title: Night Cruise Overture
comment:
# Night Cruise Overture

Orchestral piece in the style of 80s Japanese city pop, at 112 BPM in 4/4, 74 bars (about 2:39). It is in E♭ with the last chorus a half step up in E, and the turnaround slides back to the top for the loop.

## Form

| Section | Bars | Chords | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Intro | 1–8 | A♭maj7, G7♭9, Cm7, B♭m7–E♭7, then ending Cm7–F7, Fm7–B♭7sus4 | Glockenspiel teases the chorus hook over harp and string pads; groove and brass enter at bar 5 |
| Verse | 9–24 | E♭maj7, Cm7, Fm7, B♭13, Gm7, C7♭9, Fm7, B♭7sus4, then ending A♭maj7, Gm7, Fm7–Gm7, A♭maj7–B♭7sus4 | Flute melody over a light groove; it climbs in the second half with the clarinet an octave down |
| Pre-chorus | 25–32 | A♭maj7, B♭/A♭, Gm7, Cm7, Fm7, Gm7–C7, A♭maj7–A♭m6, B♭7sus4–B♭7♭9 | Horns and clarinet carry a longer-note melody; the groove goes to full 16ths |
| Chorus | 33–48 | A♭maj7, G7♭9, Cm7, B♭m7–E♭7 ×4 | Violins and flute play the hook in unison; brass stabs, timpani pushes each cycle |
| Brass interlude | 49–56 | A♭maj7, Gm7, Fm7, B♭7sus4, A♭maj7, Gm7–C7, F♯m7–B7sus4, Bm7–E7♭9 | Trumpet line with the trombone an octave below; the last two bars slide down into E |
| Last chorus (E) | 57–72 | Amaj7, G♯7♭9, C♯m7, Bm7–E7 ×4 | Violins in octaves, glockenspiel sparkle, trumpet joins the melody in the second half |
| Turnaround | 73–74 | Amaj7, B♭m7–E♭7 | Flute holds the maj7, then a ii–V back to the intro in E♭ |

## Tracks

| Track | Part |
| --- | --- |
| Flute | Verse melody, chorus hook |
| Clarinet | Verse doubling, pre-chorus melody |
| Violins | Chorus hook, pads |
| Horns | Pre-chorus melody, pads |
| Trumpet | Interlude lead, last chorus melody |
| Trombone | Interlude line an octave below |
| Brass Section | Stabs pushing the "and" of 4 |
| Glockenspiel | Hook tease and sparkle, standing in for DX7 bells |
| Harp | Arpeggios and build-up glissandos |
| Pizzicato | Offbeat 16th chops, like a cutting guitar |
| Low Strings | Sustained pad throughout |
| String Runs | Scale runs into sections |
| Pizz Bass | Octave-popping 16th bass |
| Contrabass | Bowed weight in the bigger sections |
| Timpani | Downbeats, chorus pushes, rolls |

## Groove and harmony

- There is no drum kit, so the groove comes from pizzicato basses popping octaves, pizzicato chops on the offbeats, and brass stabs pushing the "and" of 4.
- The chorus uses the IVmaj7–III7–vim7–v7–I7 "Just the Two of Us" progression.
- Each section boundary gets a build scaled to the lift: a string run, a timpani roll on the dominant, a harp glissando, and bass pedals in 8ths. The biggest go into the choruses and back into the loop.
